lens_full: Hidden-state auditor: can the fresh-process replay be satisfied by leaked in-process state (REGISTRY mutation, PxC pre-seeding, results aliasing), and does the child's sys.path/PYTHONPATH discipline hold?
retained: ATTACK 1a (mutate calculations.REGISTRY AFTER retain, before replay) is DEFEATED. Ran: swap REGISTRY['fn.ablation.compare'] = REGISTRY['fn.ablation.split'] with the honest record in hand. In-process retain.replay raised KeyError 'rows' (the mutation bites); the fresh child returned failed_checks [], result_digests == record['results'] True, and evidence/replay/fresh-process.log ended 'VERDICT: accepted' -- the child imports its own calculations module from disk (replay.py CHILD_REPLAY_SNIPPET line 182 'from calculations import REGISTRY'), so the parent's dict is invisible to it. This is what test_replay.py:281 already asserts; reproduced independently.

ATTACK 1b (mutate REGISTRY BEFORE retain, so the poisoned record reaches disk) is DEFEATED. Ran: REGISTRY['fn.ablation.score'] = Calculation('fn.ablation.score', flat_score) (a named module-level function, no lambda), then replay.ensure_retained_record() -> the poisoned record was written and differs from the honest one. Refusal: "child failed checks ['provider_agrees', 'calculations_source_matches_record']; child returncode 3; result digests differ from record['results']". Three independent checks fired, not one. evidence/run-1/retained.json was snapshotted before the probe and restored byte-for-byte.

ATTACK 2 (pre-seed Parts into the child's PxC) is DEFEATED in all four shapes constructed. The child's PxC is built only inside retain.replay (retain.py:633-637); there is no parent-supplied board. 2a extra external 'input.ablation.smuggled' -> refused on externals_match_declared_inputs. 2b value-forged DECLARED external (make_data(8,400)) with every digest recomputed so the record is self-consistent -> passed all four child checks and was refused by the PARENT on 'comparison rows differ from the committed comparison.json'. 2c pre-seed of an into address hidden behind the {'digest','ref'} sidecar shape that retain.py:635-636 skips -> child crashes in PxC.get (core.py:58-59) and the parent logs 'VERDICT: refused (child produced no JSON report)'. 2d swap the two declared externals' values -> same. check_record (retain.py:507-513) plus the child's externals check plus the parent's row check cover the space.

ATTACK 3 (results aliasing) cannot forge a fresh-child accept. pcr.py:334-336 does publish one object as both run.results[id] and the PxC value, and the aliasing is real and observable (see the finding on the two digest columns) -- but both retain_run and a replay digest the SAME post-run object graph, so an in-place mutation is reproduced identically on both sides rather than creating a gap a forger can sit in. Separately: pyto.core.PxC holds no class-level state (core.py:49-51, both dicts are per-instance), so there is no cross-PxC channel to pre-seed either.

sys.path / PYTHONPATH discipline HOLDS. In the committed evidence/replay/fresh-process.log, sys.path after minus sys.path before == ['/home/user/DiscStudio-staging/pyto/experiments/grouped-ablation'] -- exactly one inserted intra-repo directory, and it is the experiment dir (test_replay.py:241-243). env is {'PATH': ...} only (replay.py:113, test_replay.py:235-239) and the spawn uses -I (replay.py:325), which implies -E, so no PYTHONPATH reaches the child. Disclosure note, not a defect: '/home/user/DiscStudio-staging/pyto/src' is ALSO on the child's path, put there by the editable install's __editable__.pyto_lab-0.1.0.pth in dist-packages, not by an insert. That is the mechanism CAPTURE.md's sys.path section explicitly requires ('the library is reached through the editable install on Days 1-4 ... never by pointing at pyto/src') and it is printed verbatim on the log's 'sys.path before' line.

Byte-equality of the Day 2 seam independently reproduced (not taken from the lane's own tests): json.dumps([asdict(t) for t in run.ticks]) is identical with observe=True and observe=False on the Day 1 program; run.receipts == {} when observe is not passed; one receipt per invocation when it is; and those bytes equal evidence/run-1/testimony.json['ticks'] (which is {pcr, ticks} only).

bash scripts/check_all.sh exits 0 on the working tree: library 64, experiments/grouped-ablation 170, experiments/s3-synthetic 5, consumer 61, disc-stats 4, examples 3, art-registry-md OK. ALL SUITES PASSED.

findings.claim: The fresh-process log's module-leak check is a DELTA over new_modules, so any module already resident in the child's sys.modules when the snippet starts is never audited -- and two such modules are resident in the committed evidence. The docstring's claim that the module dump is 'the proof that nothing beyond pyto + calculations (+ features) + retain was on the child's module table' is false as written.
findings.evidence: replay.py:358-363 computes `leaked` from report['new_modules'] only, and test_replay.py:245-251 repeats the same formula; report['sys_modules_before'] (replay.py CHILD_REPLAY_SNIPPET line 170) is written into the log and then never checked against _ALLOWED_TOP_LEVEL_MODULES (replay.py:474-478). Applying that same formula to sys_modules_before in the COMMITTED logs: evidence/replay/fresh-process.log and evidence/replay/fresh-process-run-2-regroup.log both yield ['__main__', '_distutils_hack', 'sitecustomize'] -- i.e. site-packages code that executes in the 'fresh' child before any of the four checks -- while log line 19 reads 'new modules outside {pyto, calculations, features, retain}: []'. Reproduced end to end by prefixing replay.CHILD_REPLAY_SNIPPET verbatim with three lines injecting sys.modules['smuggled_provider'] and spawning it with the parent's exact argv/env/-I -B; result: returncode 0, failed_checks [], parent's leak formula over new_modules -> [], same formula over sys_modules_before -> [..., 'smuggled_provider'], and 'smuggled_provider' present in the final sys_modules. A pre-loaded fake `retain` would likewise be invisible. (Scoped honestly: `import sitecustomize` resolves to /usr/lib/python3.11/sitecustomize.py, ahead of pyto/src on the child's startup path, so this channel needs system-level write, not repo write -- which is why this is major and not a blocker.)
findings.required_fix: In replay.py compute `leaked` over report['sys_modules'] rather than report['new_modules'], subtracting an explicitly named startup-resident set, and add a check that 'pyto', 'calculations', 'features' and 'retain' are ABSENT from report['sys_modules_before'] (fold both into the VERDICT reasons at replay.py:401-414 and print both lines). Mirror both assertions in test_replay.py::FreshProcessReplay. Then either narrow the replay.py:279-280 docstring to what the delta actually proves, or keep the claim and make the full-table check back it.
findings.short_summary: Module-leak check audits only new_modules, not the resident table

findings.claim: The documented 'Close it by (orchestrator, after this round is merged, on a clean tree)' procedure for the -dirty stamp provably cannot produce the result it promises. Run on a pristine clone of HEAD, it yields a bare sha for run-1 only; runs 2, 3 and 4 get '-dirty', and the final `python3 replay.py` rewrites run-1's own retained.commit back to '-dirty'.
findings.evidence: Executed the exact five commands in the item's close-it block on a clean `git clone --shared` of HEAD 64d887b (0 uncommitted changes at start): run-1/commit.txt = '64d887b84157d2d2e3b2e9bdbe94137defcded49' (bare); tree dirt after run.py = 5 files; run-2-regroup/commit.txt, run-3-reinput/commit.txt, run-4-from-retained/commit.txt all = '...defcded49-dirty'; and after `python3 replay.py`, run-1/retained.json retained.commit = '...defcded49-dirty'. Cause: WATCHED_PATHS is (HERE, SRC_DIR) (run.py:55) -- the whole experiment directory, evidence/ included -- while write_evidence excludes only the CURRENT out_dir (run.py:290), so each run's freshly written evidence is dirt for the next run, and replay.main() rewrites evidence/run-1/retained.json (replay.py:886) after the other three runs have dirtied HERE. The item's own success criterion ('confirm every evidence/*/commit.txt is 40 hex characters with no suffix') is unreachable in one pass.
findings.required_fix: Either widen the exclusion at run.py:290 to the whole evidence/ tree -- the comment two lines above already states the principle, 'never count the evidence directory itself as dirt: outputs are not the code that produced them' -- or rewrite the OPEN-FINDINGS close-it block to say the operator must `git commit` between each of the five commands and that a single pass can only clear run-1. Do not leave a procedure in the ledger that an owner will run and find cannot close.
findings.short_summary: OPEN-FINDINGS close-it procedure cannot produce a bare sha

findings.claim: Running the day's own verification rewrites the day's own committed evidence: a single `bash scripts/check_all.sh` on a clean tree leaves 13 committed evidence files modified. The tests that read those files read the copy they just regenerated, so the COMMITTED fresh-process logs and retained.json are never actually verified by the suite.
findings.evidence: On the pristine clone of HEAD (0 changes before), one check_all.sh run left exactly: evidence/replay/{forged-record-refused,fresh-process,fresh-process-run-2-regroup,fresh-process-run-3-reinput,fresh-process-run-4-from-retained}.log, evidence/replay/refusals/{digest-forged,module-leak,registry-forged,source-sha-mismatch,value-forged-rows}.log, evidence/run-1/retained.json, evidence/tamper/{mutating-baseline-refused-record,retained-tampered}.json -- 13 files, verified with `git status --porcelain`. FreshProcessReplay.setUpClass (test_replay.py:163-165) calls replay.ensure_retained_record() (which write_record()s evidence/run-1/retained.json, replay.py:159) and replay.run_fresh_process_replay() (which rewrites FRESH_PROCESS_LOG, replay.py:416) before every assertion in the class, and the log's 'cwd (outside repo): /tmp/replay-cwd-XXXX' line is a new tempfile.mkdtemp name on every run (replay.py:318, 337), so the bytes differ each time by construction.
findings.required_fix: Split regeneration from verification: keep `python3 replay.py` as the producer, and make test_replay.py assert against the committed artifacts without rewriting them (e.g. build the record and log into a temp dir and compare bytes to the committed ones, the way test_second_experiment.py::CommittedLedgers already reads run-1/receipts.json read-only). At minimum, make the run-varying tempdir path stop appearing in the committed log so a re-run is a byte no-op, and state in CAPTURE.md that check_all is expected to leave the evidence tree unmodified.
findings.short_summary: check_all.sh rewrites 13 committed evidence files it then asserts on

findings.claim: Every evidence directory carries two per-invocation digest columns -- receipts.json[*].result_sha256 and retained.json['results'][*] -- that an owner will read as the same measurement. They are equal in all four committed runs today, but they are computed at different moments over an aliased object, and nothing in the repository asserts the relationship or names the difference.
findings.evidence: pcr.py:357 computes result_sha256 immediately after the call, inside the per-invocation loop; retain.py:597 computes digest_of(value) over run.results AFTER the whole run has finished. pcr.py:334-336 publishes one object as both results[id] and the PxC value, so a Calculation that mutates an upstream result in place makes the two disagree. Measured now: across evidence/run-1 (15 ids), run-2-regroup (11), run-3-reinput (15), run-4-from-retained (14), zero mismatches. Demonstrated the divergence with a named module-level Calculation (no lambda) that zeroes args['model']['w'] before scoring: 6 of 15 ids diverged -- fit.all a130f380b6a3a4c7 (post-run) vs 339d487ebda66283 (receipt), fit.drop_g0 64fbb7e5db0a93a4 vs c3dbf808b5a18abe, and likewise drop_g1/g2/g3/g4 -- and retain_run wrote the post-run (mutated) digest for every one of them. `grep -rn result_sha256 --include=*.py experiments/ consumers/` returns nothing: no test pins the two columns together, and retain.py:28's record shape says only "results {invocation id: sha256 | None}".
findings.required_fix: Add a test over the committed runs asserting record['results'][id] == receipts[id]['result_sha256'] for every id in each of the four evidence directories -- it passes today and fails the first time an in-place mutation appears -- and amend retain.py:28 (and retain_run's docstring at retain.py:541) to say that `results` digests each value as it stood at the END of the run, citing pcr.py:334-336 for why that can differ from the receipt's production-time digest.
findings.short_summary: Two per-invocation digest columns agree by luck, pinned by nothing

findings.claim: A machine-absolute path is baked into a module the consumer suite imports, so check_all.sh's 'consumer 61 OK' is green only in a checkout that happens to live at /home/user/DiscStudio-staging. This is the cross-checkout reach that CAPTURE.md's sys.path section and docs/worktree-workflow.md:17 forbid, expressed as a literal instead of a sys.path insert.
findings.evidence: fixtures.py:20 is `CARD_CONSUMER_DIR = Path("/home/user/DiscStudio-staging/pyto/consumers/discstudio-card")`, and consumers/discstudio-card/test_art_registry.py:62-66 inserts the harness directory and does `import fixtures`, using fixtures.PALETTES (:75) and fixtures.SAMPLE_CARDS (:157). Running scripts/check_all.sh from a clean `git clone --shared` of HEAD in a scratch directory failed the consumer suite outright: "ImportError: 'test_card_composition' module incorrectly imported from '/home/user/DiscStudio-staging/pyto/consumers/discstudio-card'. Expected '<clone>/pyto/consumers/discstudio-card'" -- the clone's suite silently reached back into this machine's tree. Pre-existing: the file was added at d9dded6, the Day 2 base commit, and it is outside Day 2's permitted file set, so this is for routing rather than for this day's fixer.
findings.required_fix: Derive CARD_CONSUMER_DIR from __file__ (Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3] / 'consumers' / 'discstudio-card') so the harness resolves inside whatever checkout is running, and add the absolute-path pattern to the isolation lens that already greps tests.txt for PYTHONPATH and sys.path.insert (experiments/CAPTURE.md, 'sys.path: what is logged and what is forbidden').
findings.short_summary: Hardcoded absolute repo path makes the consumer suite non-portable
